candidates.hypothesis: In swap_vma_ra_win and swap_update_readahead, requiring 2+ contiguous hits before expanding win > 1 and immediately collapsing win = 1 on non-contiguous access eliminates speculative swap readahead on random workloads while retaining sequential readahead throughput. Reject if sequential throughput degrades significantly, or if random p99 tail latency fails the calibrated noise guard.

mechanism.claim: In mm/swap_state.c, readahead window expansion win > 1 is gated on 2+ consecutive contiguous page faults (faddr == prev_faddr ± PAGE_SIZE); any stride disruption or random access immediately collapses win = 1 and resets streak to 0, preventing speculative I/O from inflating random tail latency.
mechanism.falsifier: Exact-tree review shows lost lifetime protection, incorrect slot conflict handling, or broken cache lookup fallback. Correctness, metadata spread <1%, and calibrated fast-tier screen independently gate execution.

decision.complexity_justification: Gating swapin readahead expansion on verified sequential stride and immediately collapsing to win=1 on non-contiguous access adds algorithmic branch checks in the swapin fault path, which slightly increases test burden across access patterns while eliminating speculative I/O on random access.

decision.reason: Candidate achieves FAST_PASS with reduced random swapin latency (-0.96% mean disk, -6.4% zram p99) and passing scored guardrails across all 4 screening pairs.
decision.learning_value: Demonstrates that streak gating (requiring 2+ contiguous hits before win > 1) and immediate collapse to win=1 eliminates speculative readahead on random workloads, improving random tail latency while introducing a small (+1.27%) sequential disk readahead expansion ramp delay.
